title: Finite refinement makes the positive-degree bottom comparison colimit invertible
statement: Let X be qcqs, A a Grothendieck abelian category, F an A-valued small-etale sheaf and q a positive integer. On the actual filtered homotopy-cohomology diagram [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-hypercover-model], the colimit mediator into the explicitly constructed injective-resolution comparison cocone [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-hypercover-comparison-cocone] is an isomorphism. No arbitrary comparison map is selected: this is colimit.desc of comparisonCocone A F q.

source.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 1: hypercover computation, finite staircase through degree q+1; Stacks Tag 01H0 first proof

proof.text: Use the already constructed section bicomplex and canonical comparison cocone. The resolution augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by the proved injective-row theorem.

Filter the first-quadrant total complex by resolution degree. In total degree q, work only through q+1. Exactness of the resolution is local on the finitely many hypercover constituents. Refine their matching covers to obtain local lifting diagrams and carry out the finite descending staircase: subtract boundaries to remove positive resolution-degree components. This proves local surjectivity of the bottom comparison. Apply the same finite staircase to a primitive to prove local vanishing of its kernel. These are statements about categorical images, kernels, and finite sums in A, not an assumption that A has a projective generator. This is the categorical form of the finite correction argument in [lem-sc-hypercover-bottom-refinement-descent].

The cohomology diagram, rather than the raw complex diagram, is filtered after homotopy quotienting. Apply AB5 to the resulting image/kernel statements and conclude the canonical colimit mediator is both mono and epi, hence an isomorphism.
